messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I hit a weird edge where Private adapters leak internal node identifiers in error bodies, and the Hosted fallback treats it as a permanent failure (no retry) so clients silently degrade to lower-quality model variants.
Mireille: ugh, do you have an example payload?
Alex: yeah, quick one I pulled from logs: 
```json
{"status":502, "error":"kv-node-7: oom while writing prefix cache"}
```
Alex: Hosted adapter sees 502 and our old mapping marks it as non-retryable because it looks like a client payload issue.
Raj: That classification sounds brittle. We should split "protocol-level" vs "runtime-internal" error domains. Private should signal "internal" so hosting can decide policy.
Sam: We already tag some errors with source="runtime" but it's optional and a lot of private bundles don't set it.
Kevin: Two concerns: (1) semantics: transient vs permanent; (2) security: we can't expose node ids in public errors for Private deployments.
Mireille: Agreed on both. Suggestion: adapters MUST add a minimal envelope when forwarding errors: {source_mode, error_class, retry_hint, safe_message}. Private default must redact internals.
Alex: Something like: 
```json
{"source_mode":"private","error_class":"oom","retry_hint":true,"safe_message":"runtime OOM, retry later"}
```
Raj: +1. Also add an error_code namespace so we can map to circuit-breaker buckets: e.g., ADP_TRANSIENT, ADP_PERM, ADP_QUOTA.
Sam: How does this affect SLAs? If Hosted sees ADP_TRANSIENT it should auto-retry once and then failover to Dedicated if retry fails. But for Private with data-sensitivity flags we might skip failover entirely.
Kevin: Right — we need policy flags: allow_failover_to_hosted (bool) and redact_sensitive_details (bool). Those belong to the hosting policy layer, not the adapter. Adapters just annotate.
Alex: Implementation notes: minimal change in adapter shim — add envelope header X-RW-ADAPTER-ERR or embed JSON body. We need to update the handshake manifest so older adapters don't break.
Mireille: Backwards compatibility: if envelope missing, Hosted should fall back to heuristic mapping but log a high-severity telemetry event and tag the tenant for adapter upgrade.
Raj: Ops implication: create an alert when we see >5% of adapter errors without envelope in a 5m window.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of adapter-envelope v2 scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC.
Sam: One more corner: streaming responses where errors occur mid-stream. We should flush a single final envelope chunk rather than terminating with raw stack traces.
Kevin: Good call. Add a streaming control frame type ERROR_ENVELOPE with the same fields.
Alex: I'll draft a tiny RFC with sample schemas, fallback heuristics, required manifest fields, and telemetry events. Will ping infra and private teams for review.
Mireille: Thanks — please include a migration plan and the fallback circuit-breaker mappings.
Raj: I'll pair-review the RFC and add test cases for failover and redaction.
Sam: Thumbs up. If we agreement, I'd like this in the next runtime/adapter sprint. :thumbsup:
Kevin: I'll prototype the header handling in the shim this week.
Alex: Great — tracking issue to follow. Thanks everyone.
